reasoning: The core problem — whether stacked LLM control monitors miss independently or share correlated failures, and how correlation inflates the true stacked false-negative rate above the naive independence (FNR)^N prediction — is directly addressed by multiple existing works. "Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety" (arXiv:2507.15886) explicitly identifies correlated monitor failures, contrasts them with the independence assumption, and empirically validates combined-monitor protocols. Most on-point, the SPAR "Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control" work (LessWrong + arXiv:2605.15377) runs many LLM monitors over attack trajectories and measures diversity precisely as the inverse of average pairwise correlation in suspicion scores on attack samples, showing anti-correlation drives ensemble detection gains — essentially the proposal's hit/miss correlation matrix on the same class of datasets (Control Arena/APPS). The proposal's distinct framing (importing reliability-engineering common-cause analysis, phi/Q-statistic on a binary miss matrix, and explicitly quantifying the observed-vs-independence FNR gap on public malign trajectories like SHADE-Arena) is a modest delta rather than an unexplored problem; the gaps are minor.

evidence.title: Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety (2507.15886)
evidence.summary: Develops an algorithm to combine multiple monitors of varying cost/performance. Explicitly raises correlated monitor failures and the naive independence assumption (probability no monitor flags = FNR^N), noting an agent can correlate failures (e.g. same jailbreak across instances) which breaks independence. Empirically more than doubles recall vs a naive baseline in a code-review setting. Covers the proposal's central concern about independence breaking down.

evidence.title: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh Scale (arXiv:2605.15377, SPAR)
evidence.summary: Runs 12 LLM monitors (7 prompt variants + 4 fine-tunes) over attack trajectories on APPS Control Arena and BigCodeBench-Sabotage, and measures monitor diversity as the inverse of average pairwise correlation in suspicion scores computed on attack samples only. Shows that selecting anti-correlated (diverse) monitors yields 2.4x greater detection gain than equal-compute baselines. Most directly overlaps the proposal's per-trajectory hit/miss correlation analysis; credible authors (SPAR program) with open code and arXiv paper.

evidence.title: Practical challenges of control monitoring in frontier AI deployments (2512.22154)
evidence.summary: Notes that monitoring protocols fail when the probability of flagging an attack is too low because per-step recall is low, attacks involve few steps, or monitor scores are correlated across steps. Directly identifies correlated monitor scores as a key failure mode undermining defense-in-depth, the proposal's premise.

evidence.title: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures? (2510.11235)
evidence.summary: Frames the exact conceptual question the proposal poses — whether layered/stacked safety mechanisms fail independently or exhibit shared (common-cause) failures — at a risk-modeling level, establishing that the independence-vs-correlation question for stacked defenses is already an active research framing.

evidence.title: Adaptive Attacks on Trusted Monitors Subvert AI Control Protocols (2510.09462)
evidence.summary: Shows adaptive prompt-injection attacks can fully subvert monitor-dependent control protocols, inducing low suspicion on clearly malicious actions. Demonstrates a concrete common-cause mechanism (shared semantic vulnerability) that makes monitor misses correlated across layers, supporting that the correlated-miss phenomenon is already documented.
